description.narrative: GNBCC and the Netherland Embassy in Accra have a collective goal of contributing to the development of the private sector and increasing the bilateral trade flows between the Netherlands and Ghana focusing on horticulture, cocoa, diaspora, women in business, and youth. The digital research study is therefore conducted to understand digital communication usage and their most effective communication channels among selected groups within the involved business value chain and groups.

description.narrative: The study will primary seeks to understand the digital communication platform of each of the groups in order to device a strategic digital marketing approach when engaging them. For instance young entrepreneurs are best reached by Instagram, business women could preferably be reached by Facebook (FB) and the Dutch businessmen through a digital trade office or other preferred channels. The current study will bring to light the digital communication channels of each of these target groups and inform policy on the most effective digital communication channels to reach and engage with them.

description.narrative: "The study examined the digital communication channels of specific target groups in Ghana and the most effective communication channels to reach them. The study evidenced that the majority (61.2%) of the respondents had 24-hour daily internet access providing a clear indication that the respondents are mostly online. The study also showed evidence that a majority (66.9%) of the respondents use their mobile phones as their medium of internet access and a reasonable number of the respondents use a combination of their laptops and their mobile phones as their mode of internet access. For challenges in internet access two challenges were mostly encountered by the respondents; high cost of internet bundle as well as network challenges. For the internet use and content viewed online, there were multiple contents viewed online the content consumed among the respondents are; (1) Reading of news and keeping up with information on the internet (66.8%), (2) Entertainment (videos, music, clips, etc) (49.3%), (3) Finding jobs, talents, and skills needed for job and company (48.8%), (4) Communication with friends and others online (54.5%) and (5) making new friends and socializing (37.8%). The most preferred communication platform used by the target group was one of the key objectives investigated by the study; respondents to some extent pre-ferred face-to-face engagement when it comes to business discussions (23.8%). For online communication platforms, the most dominant platforms used by the respondents included Facebook pages, Facebook lives, and Facebook groups. Whatsapp was also favored by some of the respondents. However, according to the Ghana Dig-ital Report (2020), the top five most used internet platforms in Ghana comprise; Whatsapp, Facebook, Youtube, Instagram, and FB Massagers. A breakdown of the findings revealed that 53.7% of women in business prefer face-to-face and 42.1% of young entrepreneurs also prefer face-to-face. For online communication channels, women in business prefer to use Facebook live (8.4%) and Facebook pages (9.5%). The young entrepreneurs however prefer LinkedIn (19.3%) and Telegram (9.1). For Ghanaian businesspeople, they prefer Facebook live (15.1) and Linked in (23.0%). The Dutch business community predominately access relevant information online using their mobile phones. They are on social media platforms and access relevant information through google searches, government information websites, and social media platforms. Some also use private portals and chambers of commerce. LinkedIn was prominent when it comes to hiring and reaching out to new talents for most of them. Some also use their Ghanaian networks through email and some also use recruitment agencies. Digital trade office: This was considered by the Dutch community as a useful platform that will aid in their regular search for business information. The portal if combined with the government and other related official sources will provide useful value to the community. The Diaspora community, just like the Dutch business community, is also active online and uses social media, especially LinkedIn to reach out to new talents and connect with others. They mostly use business websites in addition to social media platforms to access information and do business. For determining the platform for linking with fast-growing companies, the study revealed that all three target groups preferred the use of social media platforms; 70.5% of all the women in business prefer social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, etc, 85.3% of young entrepreneurs, and 75.4% of all the Ghanaian busi-ness persons. On the final research objective, examining the mix of channels that will reach the majority of the target groups, for all the target groups (Women in business, Young entrepreneurs, and Ghanaian Businesspeople) the use of Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, Email and a combination of a phone call and an online social media ad cam-paign can reach up to about 90% of the respondents based on the current platforms used by the respondents. "
